help.balance: Budget works out your balance: your starting balance, plus your income, minus your expenses. Compare it with your bank now and then. If they differ, a transaction is probably missing.
help.budgets: A budget is the amount you plan to spend on something each month, like Groceries. Budget shows how much of it is left, and turns red only when you spend more.
help.buffer: A safety buffer is money that always stays in your savings, for surprises like a broken washing machine. Anything above it is free to spend.
help.carry: Carry over: money you don't spend this month is added to that budget next month. Without it, the budget starts again at its amount, and what's left can go to your savings.
help.fit: Your income minus your budgets. What's left can go to your savings or bigger plans. Below zero, you plan to spend more than comes in.
help.free: What you can spend from your savings without dropping below your safety buffer, now or in any month ahead.
help.noBudget: Spending you didn't put on a budget. It still counts: it comes on top of your budgets.
help.outlook: The Outlook looks a year ahead: your expected income, your budgets and planned costs like a holiday, and what that means for your savings each month.
help.ready: In the last week of the month, Budget checks whether your bank account will hold next month's budgets, counting the income you still expect this month.
help.startingPoint: The balance you start from. You don't need to enter older transactions: everything you add from that day on is counted on top of it.
